clue.text: Bottomless wine cask for old musician

definitions.note: the answer names an old instrument; the clue stands it for the person playing it

indicators.note: something bottomless has lost its base, so the last letter of the following word is cut away

blocks.note: sack is an old name for a dry white wine from Spain
a butt is a large barrel for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A drained barrel of wine is handed to some bygone minstrel.
explanation.walkthrough: SACKBUT is the Renaissance ancestor of the trombone; here the instrument stands for its player.
explanation.definitionFit: A sackbut is an early slide brass instrument, so its player is a musician from centuries past.

clue.text: Moderate appeal for love

blocks.note: SOS is the distress call, an urgent appeal for help
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A gentle plea for affection, nothing too passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means middling or mediocre, neither good nor bad, which is what moderate can mean.

clue.text: The noisy bird in the tribe died and went to ... heaven?

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so the bird goes within the tribe's letters

blocks.note: a clan is a tribe or extended family group
noisy is LOUD, and the bird is the cuckoo, famous for its call
D is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A raucous bird among its people dies and goes to its reward.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this heaven is a fanciful one; the phrase comes from Aristophanes' comedy The Birds, where birds build a city in the clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloud-cuckoo-land is an imaginary ideal realm of fantasy, a dreamer's paradise, hence a whimsical sort of heaven.

clue.text: Left the bar, ordered by the wife

indicators.note: letters that are ordered are being arranged anew, so these words are put into a different sequence

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: A man quits the pub because his wife has told him to.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a henpecked husband obeying orders; 'ordered' is really the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Better half is a jocular, affectionate idiom for one's spouse, traditionally used by a husband of his partner.

clue.text: Solver's one right to enter two points on court

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the next pieces are placed within the solver's word

blocks.note: the setter addresses the solver as 'thou', so the solver's is the old possessive thy
Roman numeral one
RT is a standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The solver is told to step onto a tennis court for a couple of points.
explanation.walkthrough: THY holds I and RT: TH-IRT-Y gives THIRTY.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring, a player who has won two points in a game has thirty, after fifteen for the first.

clue.text: Born with a skin disease, being without energy, I take calls

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the sufferer's word wraps round the energy symbol

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for born
a leper is someone with leprosy, which attacks the skin
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone born with a skin complaint and lacking vigour sits answering the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking: LE-E-PER after B gives BLEEPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeper is a pager, a small device that receives calls and beeps; the clue lets the gadget speak for itself.

clue.text: Large cake: large roll's possibly as hot inside

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters could be arranged in some other way
inside places the rearranged letters within the bread roll's word

blocks.note: a bap is a large soft bread roll in Britain
taken as written

explanation.surface: At a bakery, a big cake and a big roll both come out of the oven hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cake' looks like baking, but soap is sold in cakes; the bakery picture continues the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap comes in bars traditionally called cakes, and a big one for the tub is bath soap.

clue.text: Nothing in Vermeer's work is for good

indicators.note: a painter's work is something made, so the painter's name is worked into a new arrangement
in places the nothing symbol within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: the Dutch painter's name, taken as written
nothing is zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: An art critic declares Vermeer's paintings lasting masterpieces, nothing in them temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore means always or for all time, matching the idiom for good, meaning permanently.

clue.text: Expert and lay climber's link keeping pet No. 4 in prophetic style

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase describing a manner, matching the adjective answer

indicators.note: in a down entry a climber goes upwards, so the word for lay is read from the bottom up
keeping means holding inside, so the link word holds the pet and the number

blocks.note: a pro is a professional or expert
a lay is a ballad or song
a tie is a link or bond
a cat is a typical household pet
number four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A professional and an amateur mountaineer share a rope, and somehow a pet comes along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert and lay' sets up professional against amateur, but a lay is a song. In a down clue a climber goes upwards, so the song is read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To prognosticate is to foretell the future, so something prognosticative is predictive in the manner of a prophet.

clue.text: Spitting's allowed here: decay is an endless chain

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the chain word is removed

blocks.note: rot is decay
taken as written
a chain of events is a series

explanation.surface: A sign permits spitting on the premises, and the place is rotting away.
explanation.walkthrough: Spitting sounds like rude behaviour, but it means roasting meat on a spit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a restaurant or appliance where meat is roasted on a revolving spit.

clue.text: Go away with sounds of fairy rings stealing around - damage just where one didn't want it

definitions.text: damage just where one didn't want it

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the stealing phrase wraps round the rings

blocks.note: shoo is what you say to send someone away
tones are musical sounds
an elf is a fairy creature
someone stealing is engaged in theft
two rings look like two letter Os

explanation.surface: Fairy music is shooed away, and someone sneaking round the rings gets hurt in an awkward spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stealing' is read as 'in theft', which wraps round OO: IN THEF-OO-T.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot oneself in the foot is an idiom for harming one's own interests through a self-inflicted blunder.

clue.text: See 9
ITV needs master, maybe, and we are it

definitions.text: ITV needs master, maybe, and we are it

indicators.note: maybe hints that the preceding words could form something else when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, fourteen letters

explanation.surface: The commercials themselves speak up: a TV channel depends on a master, and they are it.
explanation.walkthrough: ITV is Britain's main commercial television network, funded by commercials; the whole clue both supplies the letters and describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial broadcaster like ITV relies on paid commercials for revenue, so these are the master it serves.

clue.text: Painter of classical subjects, "The Mater Mated" possibly one

indicators.note: possibly suggests the word before it might be arranged differently

blocks.note: the best-known mater is the alma mater, so the word that goes with it stands in
taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: A painter of antiquity might well have produced a canvas titled The Mater Mated.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a painting's title; alma mater, a person's old school, supplies the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lawrence Alma-Tadema was a Victorian painter famous for lush scenes of ancient Rome and Greece.

clue.text: Commendation for being decapitated?

definitions.note: the answer is a man known for this fate, not the act itself

blocks.note: first meaning: praise
second meaning: the Archbishop of Canterbury beheaded on Tower Hill in 1645

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise for a beheading; the question mark warns that the second half is a person famous for losing his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Laud is a noun for praise, and William Laud, Charles I's archbishop, is remembered for his execution by beheading.

clue.text: Flower eaten by flea, unusual jumper

indicators.note: something eaten by another ends up inside it, so the flower sits within the insect's letters
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the insect's letters are put out of their ordinary order

blocks.note: taken as written
the iris is a flower

explanation.surface: A flower is devoured by a peculiar flea that can leap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests the flea's leaping, but it is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fair Isle is a knitted pullover in the colourful patterned style of the Shetland island of that name.

clue.text: Gather 10 on river far from 3

definitions.note: 3 is BETTER, so the definition reads far from better

blocks.note: to gather is to deduce or infer
the digits 1 and 0 resemble the letters I and O
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A cross-reference puzzle: collect entry 10 by a river, a long way from entry 3.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to the 10-across entry, but it is read as the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior means lower in quality, the opposite of better, so it is far from better.

clue.text: The Scots' own mountain covering, their own to keep

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the mountain abbreviation wraps the Scots word

blocks.note: MT is the abbreviation for mount or mountain
ain is the Scots word for own
again the Scots word for own

explanation.surface: Scots cover their mountains with their own produce and mean to keep it that way.
explanation.walkthrough: Ain is everyday Scots for own, as in 'my ain folk'.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep it going or preserve it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Serb terrorist reportedly observed behind Clinton?

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: Arkan was the nom de guerre of the Serb paramilitary leader Zeljko Raznatovic
observed is saw; the state name's ending is pronounced like this word

explanation.surface: A Serbian warlord is said to have been spotted just behind the American president.
explanation.walkthrough: The state's name is pronounced AR-kan-saw, so Arkan saw sounds the same. Bill Clinton was its governor before becoming president.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is Bill Clinton's home state, the place behind him in the sense of his background and political base.

clue.text: Colette's soldiers

blocks.note: two GIs, American soldiers

explanation.walkthrough: One plural word supplies two GIs side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is the 1944 novella by the French writer Colette, later a famous musical film.

clue.text: Spell out 4, theoretically beginning at sea

definitions.note: 4 is THIRTY; the answer is that number written out digit by digit

indicators.note: beginning means only the opening part of the long word is kept
at sea means confused or adrift, so the kept letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written; its first six letters are used

explanation.surface: Write the number out, theoretically starting from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The first six letters of theoretically, THEORE, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelling out the digits of thirty one by one gives three-oh, so the phrase is that figure written as words.

clue.text: Pursued, say (unsuccessfully, one may suppose)

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the word is matched by its pronunciation

blocks.note: pursued is chased, which is pronounced the same as the answer

explanation.surface: Someone was chased romantically, and the bracket hints the suitor got nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed comment is the definition: a pursued person who was chased without success stays virtuous.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means sexually pure or abstinent, which is how someone remains if amorous pursuit fails.

clue.text: Unwanted result of inaccurate attempt to 9 10?

definitions.text: Unwanted result of inaccurate attempt to 9 10?

blocks.note: surface reading: something one needs like nothing else, as in the idiom about not needing a thing at all
setter's reading: aiming a gun at your foot and missing upwards gives a wound much higher up

explanation.walkthrough: 9 10 is the self-harming idiom about the foot; a badly aimed shot hits higher, and the result is the thing in the saying 'I need it like ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'need it like a hole in the head' describes something utterly unwelcome, and a misfired shot could literally cause one.

clue.text: See 3
Time to die without punishment - abolish totally

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the dying word goes round the punishment

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
taken as written
the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip once used for flogging

explanation.surface: The age has come when one may die unpunished, so wipe out the penalty entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here: DI-CAT-E after ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to root out or destroy completely, so it is a synonym for wiping something out altogether.

clue.text: Hindu deity opposed to being among Muslims

indicators.note: being among a group means sitting inside it, so the letter goes within the sect's name

blocks.note: Shia Muslims form one of the two main branches of Islam
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A Hindu god is set against a Muslim community.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiva is one of the principal gods of Hinduism, the destroyer in the trinity with Brahma and Vishnu.

clue.text: Support for fire with club

blocks.note: and means together with
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Someone backs an arson attack armed with a cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is a metal stand in a fireplace that holds burning logs, one of a pair called firedogs.
